categories.name: Stream & Riparian Assessment
categories.description: Frameworks, indices and calculators for assessing stream and riparian condition.

categories.name: Ecological Modeling
categories.description: Habitat, connectivity and population models that estimate ecological outcomes of restoration alternatives.

categories.name: Hydrologic & Hydraulic Modeling
categories.description: Tools for channel hydraulics, roughness, streamflow analysis and surface water–groundwater exchange.

categories.name: Planning & Decision Support
categories.description: Economic, cost and decision analyses that pair ecological outcomes with costs.

categories.name: Data & GIS
categories.description: Map-based databases, downloadable datasets and terrain utilities.

categories.name: Training & Technical Resources
categories.description: Courses, tutorials, curated references and research tools.

resources.name: STAF
resources.description: A tiered, functions-based framework for evaluating stream condition at Screening, Rapid and Detailed levels of effort, so sites can be compared and restoration outcomes reported with consistent scoring.

resources.name: EASI
resources.description: Screening-tier (Tier 1) STAF web app: click a point on a map to delineate the watershed and reach, compute 20 stream-function metrics from public national data, and produce an ecosystem condition report.
resources.note: Screening tool, not a regulatory determination.

resources.name: SFARI
resources.fullName: Stream Functions Assessment and Rapid Index
resources.description: Rapid-tier (Tier 2) STAF field assessment: national desktop evidence supports the assessor, who scores 80 metrics across 20 stream functions to produce an ecosystem condition index.
resources.note: The Excel calculator is a draft pending Eco-PCX certification.

resources.name: DEEP
resources.description: Detailed-tier (Tier 3) STAF assessment that scores measured metric values against published reference curves, with a predefined regional assessment for each EPA Level III ecoregion.
resources.note: Regional assessments are Draft or Preliminary; none are certified.

resources.name: StreamCurves Desktop
resources.description: Windows desktop app for developing reference and regional curves for geomorphic stream metrics and building the detailed-tier assessments that DEEP runs.
resources.note: For assessment developers rather than day-to-day users.

resources.name: WARM
resources.description: Web app that helps users find, compare and run nine existing riparian assessment models through error-checked calculators.
resources.note: As of May 2025, the web app was under review for USACE certification.

resources.name: REFI
resources.description: Semi-quantitative rapid assessment of riparian condition intended for nationwide use, built around riparian effects on instream outcomes, ecological connectivity and unique habitats.
resources.note: As of May 2025, the model and its documentation were under review.

resources.name: SMURF
resources.fullName: Simple Model for Urban Riparian Function
resources.description: Rapid assessment of highly urbanized riparian zones that combines field protocols with desktop geospatial measures, developed for the Beargrass Creek ecosystem restoration study in Louisville, Kentucky.
resources.note: Model code is available on request from WRISES; documentation was in review as of May 2025.

resources.name: QHEILS
resources.fullName: Qualitative Habitat Evaluation Index for Louisville Streams
resources.description: Interdisciplinary assessment method for urban streams in the Louisville, Kentucky region that adapts the Qualitative Habitat Evaluation Index (QHEI) with geomorphic change and watershed connectivity.

resources.name: ecorest
resources.description: R package and companion web app for habitat suitability index (HSI) modeling with 300+ USFWS habitat models, plus cost-effectiveness and incremental cost analysis (CEICA).

resources.name: GSI Toolbox
resources.description: ArcGIS Pro toolbox for running habitat suitability models in a raster-based geospatial environment, with algorithms comparable to ecorest.

resources.name: WUCT
resources.description: R model that estimates quality-weighted, accessible habitat at the watershed scale to quantify benefits of removing barriers (dams, culverts, fish ladders) or impacts of new ones. Approved for national certification as a USACE planning model in October 2018.
resources.note: An R function without a graphical interface.

resources.name: PCEM
resources.description: Two-phase modeling toolkit for the Proctor Creek (Atlanta, Georgia) urban stream restoration feasibility study, combining instream, riparian, hydrologic and connectivity modules into a watershed-scale index of stream ecosystem integrity.

resources.name: NYBEM
resources.description: Model for assessing changes in habitat quantity and quality under changing hydrodynamic conditions across six coastal ecosystem types, developed for USACE coastal storm risk management studies in the New York Bight.
resources.note: As of May 2025, the documentation was in review for USACE certification.

resources.name: THREM
resources.fullName: Tidal Habitats and Resilience Evaluation Model
resources.description: Quantitative model for tidal marsh restoration in subsided former baylands of San Francisco Bay, sensitive to measures such as beneficially used material for bathymetry lifts, ecotones and refugia.

links.label: Paper on model structure and application

resources.name: RGSM Population Tool
resources.fullName: Rio Grande silvery minnow recruitment model
resources.description: Couples a 2-D hydraulic model of Middle Rio Grande floodplain inundation with an integrated population model to estimate silvery minnow recruitment under hydrologic, restoration and management scenarios.

resources.name: riverweed
resources.description: R package of functions for estimating growth of aquatic macrophytes in rivers, designed around hornleaf riverweed (Podostemum ceratophyllum) with modules that may apply to other taxa.

resources.name: HYPE
resources.description: Windows desktop app for reach-scale surface water–groundwater interaction modeling: builds and runs HEC-RAS 2D, MODFLOW 6 and MODPATH 7 models from a reach picked on a map, delineates the hyporheic zone and produces site reports.
resources.note: License terms are pending; contact the authors before redistributing.

resources.name: HyporheicTools
resources.description: Python command-line workflow and ArcGIS Pro toolbox that builds and runs MODFLOW 6 and MODPATH 7 models for hyporheic analysis from geospatial inputs, driven by a single YAML configuration.

resources.name: Hyporheic Modeling Library
resources.description: Python notebooks that automate part of a coupled workflow between HEC-RAS surface-water results and FloPy (MODFLOW 6) groundwater models for hyporheic zone assessment.

resources.name: HYDROCAL
resources.description: Combines several methods for estimating how vegetation affects channel and floodplain hydraulic roughness in one interface; originally an Excel tool, now an R package and web app.

resources.name: RHA
resources.description: Two simple tools for first-order estimates of single cross-section channel hydraulics at normal flow (trapezoidal and irregular sections), with a technical note on hydraulic analysis for stream restoration.

resources.name: Cross-Section Calculator
resources.description: Single-page web app that computes 1D open-channel hydraulics for a cross-section with Manning's equation, supporting horizontally varying n, ineffective flow areas, obstructions, levees and USGS 3DEP cross-section import.

resources.name: eRAMS Flow Analysis
resources.description: Tools on Colorado State University's eRAMS platform, developed in partnership with ERDC, that automate standard Bulletin 17B analyses of USGS streamflow gage data, visualize streamflow and compute environmental flow metrics.

resources.name: LSRI
resources.description: USACE screening-level tool that represents the relative life risk a proposed flood risk management project would reduce, used to prioritize studies and projects; ERDC contributed to parts of the framework, including the Levee and Dam Screening Tools.
resources.note: Developed with the USACE Risk Management Center.

resources.name: EngrEcon
resources.description: R package and web app for standard engineering economics calculations such as cost conversion, cash-flow analysis and life-cycle cost analysis for water resources and restoration projects.
resources.note: As of May 2025, model documentation was under review for USACE certification.

resources.name: Dam Removal Cost Estimator
resources.description: Web app that estimates dam removal costs with a machine-learning (gradient boosted) model trained on 668 dam removal projects.

resources.name: Utoy Creek Decision Support
resources.description: Case-study report applying cost-effectiveness and incremental cost analysis (CEICA) and community demographic analysis to the Utoy Creek (Atlanta, Georgia) Section 206 aquatic ecosystem restoration study.

resources.name: RESST
resources.description: Map-based web app for exploring reservoir sediment-management sites, case studies and literature, with keyword filters, a national dashboard, a searchable publication library and downloadable GIS data.

resources.name: River Engineering Resources Database
resources.description: Downloadable CSV tables behind River Engineering Resources: 188 stream assessment methods, 65 documents, 62 data and modeling tools, stream functions and a 156-metric toolbox.

resources.name: Terrain to STL
resources.description: Converts an HEC-RAS terrain HDF or a DEM GeoTIFF into a watertight STL shell for 3D printing or visualization, in the browser or with a Windows desktop app that includes an STL viewer.
resources.note: The Windows desktop bundle is unsigned.

resources.name: Using R for Ecological Modeling in USACE
resources.description: Online training book for USACE biologists, planners and analysts covering R basics, data wrangling and visualization, habitat models with ecorest, annualization, CEICA, and statistical and spatial models.

resources.name: GitHub Workflow Tutorials
resources.fullName: GitHub Skill Building Tutorials for Students & Researchers
resources.description: Step-by-step tutorial book with video walkthroughs for cloning, creating, forking and maintaining repositories and resolving conflicts using the browser, Git GUI, VS Code and RStudio.

resources.name: River Engineering Resources
resources.description: Searchable web catalog of river engineering references (documents, data and modeling tools) and 188 stream assessment methods, focused on reach-scale hydrology, hydraulics, sediment transport and geomorphology.

resources.name: ITEK Vault
resources.description: Locally installed, retrieval-augmented language model for source-grounded querying and synthesis of a curated corpus of Indigenous Traditional Ecological Knowledge (ITEK) literature.
resources.note: Intended for research and educational use; runs on your own computer.
